correctness.rationale: All positive indices are partitioned into odd, once-even and divisible-by-four cases. The first two follow from direct residues mod4 or mod8. For n divisible by four, the rational identity \(D_n-1=n^2\sum_{j\ge1}(2^j/j^2)P_j(n)\), \(\operatorname{Li}_2(2)=0\) in \(\mathbb Q_2\) and coefficient-valuation bound \(E(j,m)\) show all nonlinear terms even except the two cancelling quadratic terms \(j\in\{4,8\}\). The remaining coefficient at \(j=4\) is \(-11/3\), a 2-adic unit. The simple finite checks for \(j\le31\) and explicit high-j inequalities cover every coefficient. The included standalone verifier passes exact tests, but finite tests alone are not the proof.

originality.rationale: Lengyel (2021) explicitly poses exactly the cubic valuation as Conjecture 3 and proves only a weaker bound. The present work supplies a proof, rather than repeating the conjecture. Full relevant main statements and the exact earlier proof were inspected. Other close 2023 and 2025 work concerns different p-adic parameters or sums; targeted public mathematical-index queries found no proof of this exact conjecture. Residual risk: unindexed or uninspected later proofs may exist, so priority is not certified.

value.rationale: An explicit, unresolved conjecture in a motivated 2021 paper receives an all-index proof. The sharp exponent \(3\nu_2(n)\) strengthens a prior \(\nu_2\ge2r+2\) bound, with nontrivial cancellation and a meaningful 2-adic analytic lemma. The formula gives a complete three-case classification; it is not an arbitrary finite slice.
